subject: Mixing two models together dramatically increases sampling time

messages.author: f42b0240615306ac
messages.subject: Mixing two models together dramatically increases sampling time
parts:
Hi,

I have a ordered categorical model, that takes about 20 second for 200 sampling iterations. I want to put a known covariate matrix into it to describe cross correlations between observations. I have 600 observations, so the covariate matrix will be 600 by 600. With Cholesky factoring, this multivariate normal model itself takes about 20 seconds for 200 sampling iterations. 

However, after putting the multivariate model into the ordered categorical model, the sampling time increase to about 15 mins. So, we are talking about from 20+20 seconds to 15 mins, a 22 times increase in terms of sampling time simply by mixing two models together. Is this normal? Are there anything to improve this?

More details: the ordered categorical model and 7 parameters to estimate, the multivariate_normal itself has 600. Putting together has 607. This raises another conceptual issue, especially on the multivariate normal model, with 600 observations, and 600 parameters to estimate, is this incur the degree of freedom issue as in the frequentist point of view? Seems the bayesian side does not have this issue, but I am not clear. 

I have attached my stan model.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixing two models together dramatically increases sampling time
parts:
I didn't understand your model. Why are you Cholesky decomposing
the Kinship matrix and then multiplying it by a parameter?

The model combo behavior is not unusual. Sampling time is different than
function evaluation time. When you combine models, the geometry
can get much more difficult to navigate. What you'll see is that
the tree depth is going up.

The ordered categorical is tricky.

I take it you mean covariance matrix, not covariate matrix (which I'd probably
call "data matrix"). Did you try fitting with modeling covariance?

What happens when you get too many degrees of freedom is that you need
to control the posterior with priors. Check out the problematic posteriors
chapter of the manual for a simple example.

- Bob

P.S. I'd strongly recommend not coding the model as a string in R. You
won't be able to decode line numbers in error messages and you either have
to escape transpose or quote, depending on how you marked the string in R.
Then it can't even be cut and paste out of R.
